# 2026-604 — Quixilver: Toploader

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

## Toploader DPC serializer · transfer

### Published construction or code

A rotating capture mechanism scoops fuel from a circular plywood bucket. Rotation and up-feed have separate motors; side rollers use omni wheels. Successive fuel pushes through a corrugated-plastic tube shaped by printed ends. The bucket separates into two sections for service.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team identified serialization as the limiting process and designed the robot around it. Independent drives allow software adjustment of rotation versus up-feed.

### Engineering interpretation

The capture point moves to available fuel rather than relying solely on gravity bringing fuel to a stationary throat. Independent feed authority can help tune pile interaction and column delivery separately, but the release does not establish a universal motor-ratio setting. Bucket geometry, turret support and electronics access are part of the same flow system. Prototype rates of about 15 BPS single-stream and 23 BPS full-width are comparison claims, not sustained match scoring rates.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader chassis · drivetrain

### Published construction or code

A 27-inch square frame preserves circular bucket area without custom swerves or chamfered corners. Internal bars protect battery and module compartments; rear bumper mounts integrate armor for serializer protection.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Maximize the serializer’s available area with manufacturable hardware and protect internal mechanisms.

### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit packaging choice. It sacrifices some geometric freedom to keep the central circular feed volume useful with standard drive components. Frame perimeter, usable interior area and turret swept volume must be compared together. The team separately describes bump-only autonomous constraints; no unreviewed trench state or chassis specification should be inferred.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader inset turret · scoring

### Published construction or code

The turret is supported from above and packaged to reduce swept volume. Its sliding bearing stacks polycarbonate and aluminum plates; printed PETG spacers set clearance empirically and grease reduces friction.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Moving scoring and feeding were judged worth a lower single-stream ceiling; small swept volume preserves hopper capacity and flow.

### Engineering interpretation

A turret changes more than aiming. Its supports and swept envelope can obstruct fuel entering the serializer, so a nominal capacity comparison that ignores the moving assembly is incomplete. This release supports a manufacturable impact-tolerant bearing concept, not exact dimensions, a universal bearing preload or independently verified shot accuracy. The team’s rate trade is tied to its intended moving role.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader independently deployed arms · intake

### Published construction or code

Each intake arm uses an X44 deploy motor. Protected motors belt-drive compliant dead-axle polycarbonate rollers with silicone tubing and TPU pulley plugs. TPU belt supports retain the belts during deflection. A one-time kicker deploy uses surgical tubing and flexible plugs/string.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team explicitly connects independent deployment to eliminating the mechanically linked 2024 chain failure. Polycarbonate was preferred over SRPP to avoid permanent deformation changing belt centers.

### Engineering interpretation

Compliance must preserve transmission function, not just prevent fracture. A flexible arm changes belt geometry under load; supporting the belt during that motion is an integral part of the architecture. The team reports that TPU replaced brittle PETG roller plugs, with 100% infill and four-wall printing, and that wear still requires replacement every one or two events. Repairable consumables are not maintenance-free hardware.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader linked sliding hopper · intake

### Published construction or code

Intake deployment extends a sliding hopper; surgical tubing retracts it. Two laminated layers of corrugated plastic provide stiffness. Slots are reinforced with 0.090-inch polycarbonate sandwiched between sheets; panels use tape and adhesive for replacement.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The publication emphasizes low mass, robust sliding and easy manufacture/repair with limited router access.

### Engineering interpretation

This is a specific example of an intake–storage interface, useful to 1833’s morph chart. Linking deployment reduces independent actuation but also links faults and operating states. Slot reinforcement addresses local bearing and deformation loads that a generic corrugated-plastic wall description misses. Capacity, deflection and passage access should be measured in each loaded state; no unverified hopper capacity is assigned here.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader readiness and localization · controls

### Published construction or code

Scoring requires launch velocity, launch angle and turret yaw within tolerance plus a recent image with at least two tags. The serializer pauses when readiness fails. PhotonVision MultiTag selects camera poses using hub/total tag visibility and rejects old or ambiguous poses.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Single-driver operation reduces communication overhead; automated gating is intended to release fuel only from useful launch states.

### Engineering interpretation

Feed interruption is an intentional interface between aiming and serialization, not automatically a jam. A high mechanical BPS ceiling is useful only while readiness remains true. Logging the reason for each gating interruption would distinguish vision starvation, aim error and actual feed trouble. The release does not demonstrate those duty fractions or an electrical diagnosis of every stop.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader partner-aware bump autonomous · controls

### Published construction or code

The team describes timestamping partner paths, targeting leftover fuel after the trench race, using reusable path partials and adjustable pauses without redeployment. A Pac-Man routine is identified at NorCal DCMP playoff match 1.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

A bump-only robot was expected to reach midfield later; route selection was built around shorter partners rather than competing for the same initial race.

### Engineering interpretation

Architectural limitations can become planning inputs instead of being hidden by an ideal autonomous animation. Preserve the team’s distinction between pre-Champs crossing rules and later rules, and between experiments and actually used routines. A clever path is not proof every prototype routine competed. The release does not establish a tower mechanism; absence from the selected technical sections remains unknown, not certified absence.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

# 2026-604 — Quixilver: Toploader

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

## Toploader DPC serializer · transfer

### Published construction or code

A rotating capture mechanism scoops fuel from a circular plywood bucket. Rotation and up-feed have separate motors; side rollers use omni wheels. Successive fuel pushes through a corrugated-plastic tube shaped by printed ends. The bucket separates into two sections for service.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team identified serialization as the limiting process and designed the robot around it. Independent drives allow software adjustment of rotation versus up-feed.

### Engineering interpretation

The capture point moves to available fuel rather than relying solely on gravity bringing fuel to a stationary throat. Independent feed authority can help tune pile interaction and column delivery separately, but the release does not establish a universal motor-ratio setting. Bucket geometry, turret support and electronics access are part of the same flow system. Prototype rates of about 15 BPS single-stream and 23 BPS full-width are comparison claims, not sustained match scoring rates.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader chassis · drivetrain

### Published construction or code

A 27-inch square frame preserves circular bucket area without custom swerves or chamfered corners. Internal bars protect battery and module compartments; rear bumper mounts integrate armor for serializer protection.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Maximize the serializer’s available area with manufacturable hardware and protect internal mechanisms.

### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit packaging choice. It sacrifices some geometric freedom to keep the central circular feed volume useful with standard drive components. Frame perimeter, usable interior area and turret swept volume must be compared together. The team separately describes bump-only autonomous constraints; no unreviewed trench state or chassis specification should be inferred.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader inset turret · scoring

### Published construction or code

The turret is supported from above and packaged to reduce swept volume. Its sliding bearing stacks polycarbonate and aluminum plates; printed PETG spacers set clearance empirically and grease reduces friction.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Moving scoring and feeding were judged worth a lower single-stream ceiling; small swept volume preserves hopper capacity and flow.

### Engineering interpretation

A turret changes more than aiming. Its supports and swept envelope can obstruct fuel entering the serializer, so a nominal capacity comparison that ignores the moving assembly is incomplete. This release supports a manufacturable impact-tolerant bearing concept, not exact dimensions, a universal bearing preload or independently verified shot accuracy. The team’s rate trade is tied to its intended moving role.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader independently deployed arms · intake

### Published construction or code

Each intake arm uses an X44 deploy motor. Protected motors belt-drive compliant dead-axle polycarbonate rollers with silicone tubing and TPU pulley plugs. TPU belt supports retain the belts during deflection. A one-time kicker deploy uses surgical tubing and flexible plugs/string.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team explicitly connects independent deployment to eliminating the mechanically linked 2024 chain failure. Polycarbonate was preferred over SRPP to avoid permanent deformation changing belt centers.

### Engineering interpretation

Compliance must preserve transmission function, not just prevent fracture. A flexible arm changes belt geometry under load; supporting the belt during that motion is an integral part of the architecture. The team reports that TPU replaced brittle PETG roller plugs, with 100% infill and four-wall printing, and that wear still requires replacement every one or two events. Repairable consumables are not maintenance-free hardware.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader linked sliding hopper · intake

### Published construction or code

Intake deployment extends a sliding hopper; surgical tubing retracts it. Two laminated layers of corrugated plastic provide stiffness. Slots are reinforced with 0.090-inch polycarbonate sandwiched between sheets; panels use tape and adhesive for replacement.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The publication emphasizes low mass, robust sliding and easy manufacture/repair with limited router access.

### Engineering interpretation

This is a specific example of an intake–storage interface, useful to 1833’s morph chart. Linking deployment reduces independent actuation but also links faults and operating states. Slot reinforcement addresses local bearing and deformation loads that a generic corrugated-plastic wall description misses. Capacity, deflection and passage access should be measured in each loaded state; no unverified hopper capacity is assigned here.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader readiness and localization · controls

### Published construction or code

Scoring requires launch velocity, launch angle and turret yaw within tolerance plus a recent image with at least two tags. The serializer pauses when readiness fails. PhotonVision MultiTag selects camera poses using hub/total tag visibility and rejects old or ambiguous poses.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Single-driver operation reduces communication overhead; automated gating is intended to release fuel only from useful launch states.

### Engineering interpretation

Feed interruption is an intentional interface between aiming and serialization, not automatically a jam. A high mechanical BPS ceiling is useful only while readiness remains true. Logging the reason for each gating interruption would distinguish vision starvation, aim error and actual feed trouble. The release does not demonstrate those duty fractions or an electrical diagnosis of every stop.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader partner-aware bump autonomous · controls

### Published construction or code

The team describes timestamping partner paths, targeting leftover fuel after the trench race, using reusable path partials and adjustable pauses without redeployment. A Pac-Man routine is identified at NorCal DCMP playoff match 1.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

A bump-only robot was expected to reach midfield later; route selection was built around shorter partners rather than competing for the same initial race.

### Engineering interpretation

Architectural limitations can become planning inputs instead of being hidden by an ideal autonomous animation. Preserve the team’s distinction between pre-Champs crossing rules and later rules, and between experiments and actually used routines. A clever path is not proof every prototype routine competed. The release does not establish a tower mechanism; absence from the selected technical sections remains unknown, not certified absence.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Evidence limits

- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.

# 2026-604: Toploader September team release

Generated from `data/physical_studies.jsonl`; edit that authoritative record.

## Whole robot and packaging

A circular bucket fills much of the square chassis between standard corner modules. A rotating capture assembly sits inside it and pushes fuel up a central tube to an inset turret. The turret hangs from structure above, keeping supports out of the approaching fuel stream; its yaw envelope consumes space that would otherwise store or guide fuel. The bucket splits into two pieces, and a removable rear panel provides battery access. Separate intake arms at the front deploy a sliding hopper. Internal bars protect the battery/module compartments, and rear bumper hardware carries serializer armor. The inspected ghosted source view shows bucket, column and upper support relationships, but does not dimension the complete electrical compartment.

## Piece flow

Front rollers bring loose fuel into storage and the circular bucket. The capture assembly rotates through the available pile rather than waiting for balls to find one stationary throat. Independent up-feed rollers push captured fuel into the corrugated tube. Successive balls push the column upward into the turret; release is enabled only when launch and localization readiness are valid. The physical queue can remain occupied when the software pauses feeding.

## Annotated views

Editorial reconstruction. Not to scale; only explicit dimension labels are source dimensions. No CAD-derived measurements. Dashed envelopes are schematic and not clearance certification.

![physical-2026-604-side](../../images/physical/physical-2026-604-side.png)

## Independent arms and mechanically linked sliding walls

### Published construction

Each arm deploys with its own X44. Belt-driven dead-axle rollers use compliant construction; sliding corrugated walls deploy with the intake and retract under surgical tubing. Slots include 0.090-inch polycarbonate reinforcement.

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

### Editorial operating reconstruction

Deploy both arms and allow the walls to extend. Rollers capture fuel over the bumper into the bucket. Side-to-side compliance must preserve belt engagement even when the arms deflect differently.

### Engineering interpretation

Separate arm motors remove a rigid cross-side deployment constraint. Linking the walls still couples acquisition and storage state. Slot reinforcement carries local sliding contact instead of expecting soft wall material to hold the bearing geometry.

### Transfer and compatibility limits

This intake and low-mass wall construction can transfer independently of the turret. Keep the belt supports and wall load path; surgical tubing is a passive spring, not pneumatic actuation.

### Unknowns

Exact slot loads, belt tension across deflection and loaded retraction limits remain unknown.

### Proposed validation, not performed

First inspect the missing source interface or CAD; only then test the specific capture/transfer failure that could change the architecture. No hardware experiment was performed in this upgrade.

## Moving capture point, circular bucket and column

### Published construction

Rotation and up-feed have separate motors; side feed rollers use omni wheels. The bucket is plywood in two serviceable segments and the column is corrugated plastic held by printed ends.

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

Read cited historical note for team rationale; the operating reconstruction below is editorial and does not establish additional team intent.

### Editorial operating reconstruction

A capture feature sweeps toward loose fuel, puts it between feed contacts, and adds it to the bottom of an occupied tube. Each new ball advances the column. A ball cannot exit the top when the launcher is unavailable.

### Engineering interpretation

Rotation controls encounter rate while up-feed controls progression. Changing their ratio changes pile interaction, queue loading and the force transmitted through the ball column. That distinction is lost if both are modeled as a single feeder speed.

### Transfer and compatibility limits

The moving-capture principle can serve a fixed launcher, but changing the top outlet changes the column support and feed alignment. That adaptation is an unvalidated redesign, not a drop-in turret removal.

### Unknowns

Pocket geometry, tube clearance, compression, column force and jam reversal order are unresolved.

### Proposed validation, not performed

First inspect the missing source interface or CAD; only then test the specific capture/transfer failure that could change the architecture. No hardware experiment was performed in this upgrade.

### Published construction

### Team rationale / attribution boundary

The capture system supplies a queue, but the controller grants release only in an acceptable launch state. Loss of localization should pause release rather than be recorded as a mechanical blockage.

### Engineering interpretation

Queue control, aiming and readiness must share ownership of the next ball. A paused up-feed motor can be correct while the bucket still contains fuel; logs need a pause reason separate from jam detection.

### Transfer and compatibility limits

The yaw turret is ineligible for 1833. Velocity/angle/localization gating can transfer with chassis heading replacing turret yaw, but heading dynamics and fixed outlet geometry must be revalidated.

A central serializer that works well on the field can be costly to maintain if it traps power equipment below it. Segmentation makes access a deliberate design feature; it does not prove a particular repair time.

physical_studies.packaging: A circular bucket fills much of the square chassis between standard corner modules. A rotating capture assembly sits inside it and pushes fuel up a central tube to an inset turret. The turret hangs from structure above, keeping supports out of the approaching fuel stream; its yaw envelope consumes space that would otherwise store or guide fuel. The bucket splits into two pieces, and a removable rear panel provides battery access. Separate intake arms at the front deploy a sliding hopper. Internal bars protect the battery/module compartments, and rear bumper hardware carries serializer armor. The inspected ghosted source view shows bucket, column and upper support relationships, but does not dimension the complete electrical compartment.
physical_studies.piece_flow: Front rollers bring loose fuel into storage and the circular bucket. The capture assembly rotates through the available pile rather than waiting for balls to find one stationary throat. Independent up-feed rollers push captured fuel into the corrugated tube. Successive balls push the column upward into the turret; release is enabled only when launch and localization readiness are valid. The physical queue can remain occupied when the software pauses feeding.

source_reviews.title: Quixilver Toploader mechanical and software release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the complete team overview and later construction and service answers in the public post stream.
source_reviews.facts: Team chose a single turret despite higher full-width prototype feed rates. It details the split bucket, above-mounted turret, separately driven intake arms, and elastic sliding hopper.
source_reviews.limitations: Prototype comparisons are team-reported. Release does not quantify collision loads or match throughput.

source_reviews.title: Toploader serializer implementation
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the pinned Java source for roller commands, rotor following and jam state transitions.
source_reviews.facts: Rotor command follows filtered measured roller speed with a 1.2 surface-speed relationship. A persistent high-current and low-speed condition triggers a timed unjam command with the rotor stopped.
source_reviews.limitations: Public source defines logic and thresholds at this commit. It supplies neither as-played logs nor recovery success rates.

source_reviews.title: Toploader launch calculator implementation
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the pinned Java source for interpolated launch parameters and motion correction.
source_reviews.facts: Projects with a 50 ms latency term, evaluates velocity at the offset turret base, subtracts planar turret velocity and rotates into the tilted body frame.
source_reviews.limitations: The source does not establish calibration error under defense, nor validate the offline model against match shots.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Toploader is a single-stream moving scorer designed around its dynamic point of capture serializer. Quixilver identifies serialization as its limiting stage. It reports roughly 15 BPS in a single-stream serializer prototype and 23 in full width, then chose the turret for scoring and feeding flexibility on the move. A single driver controls the robot with automated scoring and passing logic. Its bump-only autonomous routes were designed around traffic and partner timing.
source_review.piece_flow: The front rollers deliver fuel into a sliding hopper over the circular bucket. A rotating scoop brings the capture point around the stored pile. Side omni rollers and a separately driven upfeed push successive fuel items into a corrugated-plastic tube with printed ends. New arrivals push fuel already in the column into the overhead-supported turret. The launcher uses silicone-covered PETG rollers, with recessed ties to hold the sleeve.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A 27-inch square frame preserves bucket diameter with standard-form swerve packaging. Crossbars isolate battery and module compartments and the rear bumper mount carries serializer armor. The inset turret hangs from the superstructure to keep its swept volume small and the bucket entrance open. A two-piece plywood bucket and removable rear wall section provide battery and electronics access.

subsystems.name: Independent intake and sliding hopper
subsystems.construction: Separate X44 deploy on each polycarbonate arm, belt-driven silicone-covered dead-axle rollers and TPU belt supports and pulley plugs. Laminated corrugated hopper has polycarbonate slot reinforcement.
subsystems.operation: Intake deployment pushes the hopper outward and surgical tubing retracts it. The single-deploy kicker uses an elastic drive and a string-retained, loosely fitted cross tube.
subsystems.team_rationale: Independent arms addressed chain failure on the linked 2024 design. The team wanted belt centers to recover after a hit and avoided a rigid through-bolt at the flexible tube.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Decouple impact compliance from belt retention and hopper guidance. Confirm the mechanism still closes when either side takes an off-axis hit.
subsystems.interfaces: Deploy motors to arm travel, deflecting arm to belt support, kicker plugs to string, intake to hopper slide.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Team reports TPU pulley tooth wear after one to two events and brittle PETG predecessors. Inspect the string, tooth roots and slot laminate together.
subsystems.unknowns: Deploy synchronization tolerances, force on slides and measured impact durability.

subsystems.name: Dynamic capture and column feed
subsystems.construction: Split plywood bucket, separately motorized rotating scoop and upfeed, side omni rollers, printed ends and corrugated tube.
subsystems.operation: Code averages ten roller speed samples, divides modeled roller surface speed by 1.2 and converts to rotor command. After 0.3 seconds of detected jam it stops the rotor, commands unjam velocity and resumes after 0.1 seconds.
subsystems.team_rationale: Separate drives allow tuning while omni rollers reduce lateral forces. Split bucket preserves access.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Following actual roller speed limits overdelivery during droop, but a jam downstream can leave fuel trapped above the detection point. Test with a fully packed column and minimum fill.
subsystems.interfaces: Scoop and bucket to roller, upfeed to tube, column to turret entry, and roller current and velocity to recovery state.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Code logs target and actual velocities and jam state. Inspect tube ends for distortion, and correlate retries with current and column fill.
subsystems.unknowns: Compression, full-scale success rate, wear-driven threshold drift and event firmware parity.

subsystems.name: Turret support and automated launch
subsystems.construction: Segmented polycarbonate ring, aluminum gear, PETG spacers and lubricated slider. Camera localization uses four viewpoints and multi-tag observations.
subsystems.operation: The team gates serializer feed on launch speed, elevation and yaw tolerances plus recent tag evidence. The solver interpolates a distance table for scoring, then compensates for turret motion and chassis attitude.
subsystems.team_rationale: Small swept volume protects hopper flow. Offline trajectory selection reduces onboard computation and seeks launch pairs less sensitive to errors.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Mechanical clearance and camera availability both affect firing duty cycle. Evaluate where ready-to-feed interruptions cluster before altering the table.
subsystems.interfaces: Overhead ring to rotating turret, tube to scorer, pose and velocity to aim, readiness to serializer enable.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect slider friction and play after contamination or spacer replacement. A camera view blocked by field geometry can interrupt the gate.
subsystems.unknowns: Loaded angle and speed errors, observed vision dropout and endgame hardware.

revisions: The team moved to TPU plugs after PETG impact failures. Earlier rigid aluminum tube plugs remained in one location, while cracking at another bolted tube drove the flexible TPU and string design.
transferable_principles: Compare serializers at equivalent game-piece supply and aim duty cycle. Treat service access and moving envelopes as part of the piece path.
disconfirming_conditions: A full-width approach can win the comparison if aiming opportunities are plentiful and serial delivery limits scored fuel. Pose-dependent feed gates lose value if availability is too low in intended field zones.
remaining_gaps: Controlled match-rate comparisons, as-played current traces and clearances throughout intake and turret motion remain open.
